Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Vitality Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star one to ask a question, and instructions will follow. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Vitality Brands Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Vitality Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Our discussion today will cover seven key aspects:  
1. Overall company performance highlights.  
2. Market share trends by category and region.  
3. Organic sales growth rate.  
4. Pricing actions taken and their impact on sales.  
5. Supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings impact.  
6. A&P spend and ROI.  
7. Summary of financial results and outlook.  

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more detail on our financial results.  

John Ramirez:  
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $4.8 billion, representing a 6% increase reported and 8% organic compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 53.2%, driven by productivity savings, favorable hedging, and gross margin drivers like supply chain optimizations. Operating income was $950 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.42. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Let me expand on our overall company performance highlights for the third quarter of fiscal 2024, which highlight Vitality Brands' resilience and execution amid persistent inflation, supply chain disruptions from Red Sea issues, and consumers shifting toward value and health-focused items—much like what we've observed at peers such as Procter & Gamble and Unilever. Net sales hit $4.8 billion, up 6% reported and 8% organically, after adjusting for a 1% FX headwind and 1% from last year's divestiture of a low-margin snack bar operation in North America. This extends our streak to 11 straight quarters of organic growth, powered by 4% volume increases and 4% from pricing. Our core power brands—VitalGlow skincare, PureEssence beverages, and HomeShield cleaners—making up 65% of the portfolio, surged 12% organically.  

Gross margin grew 250 basis points to 53.2%, the best in five years, thanks to $180 million in productivity savings this quarter. Our AI-driven SupplyFlow AI cut raw material waste 15% via predictive analytics on inputs like palm oil and PET resins, even as cocoa jumped 40% year-over-year. We hedged 70% of 2024 North American costs favorably, avoiding the volatility hitting Colgate-Palmolive. Operating income climbed 12% to $950 million, with margins up 120 basis points to 19.8%. Adjusted EPS rose 14% to $1.42, surpassing guidance, aided by SG&A at 24.5% of sales, down 50 basis points. Free cash flow reached $650 million, or 130% of net income, funding $400 million in buybacks and a 7% dividend hike announced today.  

Segment-wise, Health & Wellness, now 35% of sales, led with 14% organic growth. PureEssence premium protein shakes grabbed 2.2 share points in U.S. ready-to-drink per Nielsen, fueled by Ozempic trends. Beauty & Personal Care grew 7% organically, with VitalGlow hyaluronic serum boasting 25% repeat buys on DTC. Home & Fabric Care hit 5%, as HomeShield eco-pods gained in Europe under Green Deal rules. Food & Beverage was flat at 2% organic, offset by 10% in plant-based snacks in a $2 billion market growing 12% CAGR per Euromonitor.  

North America, 50% of sales, rose 9% organically on holiday pre-buys and e-commerce at 22% of mix, up from 18%, via Amazon and Walmart+. Europe advanced 6%, gaining UK laundry share per Kantar. Emerging markets, 25% of sales, jumped 12%, with India and Brazil sachets driving 8% personal care volume; our micro-dosing in Southeast Asia lifted Indonesia rural reach 18%. Under Vitality Forward 2025, we're trimming 10% of 500 SKUs to 20 high-ROIC stars, spending $500 million on microbiome probiotics for Q1 2025 launch. GenAI personalizes 40 million interactions quarterly on VitalConnect app, upping conversions 22%. M&A eyes pet nutrition, a $150 billion market at 7% growth.  

Shifting to organic sales growth rate, a core measure stripping out M&A, divestitures, and FX for pure execution visibility. Q3 organic sales advanced 4.2%, our sixth straight positive quarter, beating 3-4% guidance and topping Q3 last year's 5.1%. Nine-month YTD is 4.8%, ahead of P&G's 3.6% and Unilever's 3.2%. Power Brands, 65% of sales, drove 70% of the lift. Volume added 1.8% as pantry effects faded; price/mix 2.4% from 6-8% targeted hikes amid easing food CPI to 2.1%.  

Beauty & Personal Care, 38% of sales, grew 6.1% organically, led by FreshGlow prestige skincare and GlowBarrier serum with 12% growth on premium ASP up 15%. Beverages, 25%, hit 3.9% on Quench Zero Sugar's 18% volume and 200 bps e-comm gains. Food & Snacks, 37%, softened to 2.7% on value-pack shifts but NutriBites bars rose 14% with clean labels and 1.2% ACV up 300 points. North America shone at 5.8% with 40 bps Nielsen share gains, adding 2,500 Quench doors at 7-Eleven and 25% e-comm via Instacart. EMEA at 2.1% held pricing at 7% with 1.5% MMS in Germany Lidl. APAC 4.9% on China FreshGlow Tmall up 22%; LatAm 1.2% with Brazil Quench at 9%. Drivers: 28% sales from <3-year launches like EarthCrunch snacks at 5x velocity; 15,000 distribution points; 7.2% list prices with EDLP; GreenPack recyclables up 3% millennial lift. Q4 outlook 3.5-4.5%, full-year 4.2-4.7%.  

On pricing actions and sales impact, in this inflationary backdrop with cocoa, palm oil, PET elevated, our data-driven approach ensured top-line strength and margin defense. Q3 net sales grew 6.2% to $4.8 billion, led by 8.4% price/mix over a 2.1% volume dip—beating NielsenIQ CPG averages of 2-3%. Average 9-12% list hikes since Q4 last year, with elasticity at -0.35 via premium focus. Household: 10-11% on laundry/dish pods offsetting 15% surfactants, 9.2% price/mix, volumes -1.8% vs category -4%; EDLP cut promo volatility 15% via AI. Snacking/Beverages: 12-14% for cocoa/aluminum hits, 11.7% price/mix despite -4.2% volumes, share at 14.2% with bundles. Personal Care: 7-9%, +7.1% price/mix, flat volumes, 25% to premium. Health: +3-5%, 3.1% volume growth. North America 9.8% on 11% hikes, volumes -1.2%; Europe 7.5%, LatAm/Asia 6-8%. AI platform simulates 10,000 scenarios for 25% optimization; TPO cut ineffective spend 12% to $450M; zero-based review pruned 8% points. Q3 price/mix 7-9%, FY24 organic 4-6%.  

With that foundation, I'll turn it over to Lisa for more on brands and marketing.  

Lisa Chen:  
Thank you, John. We continue to see strong performance across our key brands. Our marketing investments are driving increased consumer engagement, and we are particularly pleased with the results of our recent Peak Protein campaign.  

Let me provide deeper insight into market share trends by category and region, reported on Nielsen/IRI basis for ACV, dollar/unit share, and velocity where available. We gained 60 basis points overall year-over-year in core channels—our 11th straight quarter—across 85% of our $25 billion+ portfolio, from volume in premiums, pricing, and 1.2 points distribution.  

By category: Snacks, 28% of sales, +150 bps globally; North America IRI +210 bps to 32.5% dollar share over Lay's/Oreo via Peak Protein bars at 15% velocity in protein snacking boom. Europe +80 bps to 18% with zero-sugar vs Aldi/Lidl. Beverages, 22%, +30 bps; U.S. premium hydration PureFlow +90 bps vs Powerade, flat CSD at 14% pivoting to adaptogens at 20% trial. Beauty & Personal Care, 19%, +70 bps; Radiance Renew +250 bps to 22% vs Lancôme, oral EnamelGuard +110 bps to 28% with 2-point penetration. Household, 18%, +40 bps; UltraClean Pods +60 bps vs Tide, eco-refills +15% velocity. Health & Wellness, 13%, +200 bps on probiotics/immunity to 12% U.S. share.  

Regions: North America 45% sales, +110 bps to 34%; e-comm PeakProtein.com +45% YoY, 3-point ACV. Europe 25%, +40 bps to 22%; Fabric +90 bps UK/Germany refill trials 25%. APAC 18%, +180 bps to 15%; China snacks +300 bps Tmall matcha, India Beauty +140 bps. LatAm 12%, +20 bps, Brazil Beverages +80 bps.  

Via Category Acceleration Playbook with Kantar/SymphonyAI: 65% gains from superior innovations targeting 20% sales <3 years old; micro-distribution 5,000 India kiranas, 10% U.S. facings; dynamic pricing +150 bps value share, premium ASP +12% Beauty; ESG 40% gains like 50% less plastic, 78% consumer preference. Q4 50-70 bps expected, backed by $1.2B marketing +8%, 95% OTIF.  

On A&P spend and ROI, Q3 total was $452 million or 14.2% of sales, +4% YoY flat constant currency, YTD $1.32B +6% organic. Promotions 62% at $280M for shopper/trade, 12% velocity lift PowerBars North America. Ads 38% $172M, digital 48% up from 38%, TV down to 22%. ROMI 2.6x up 14% via MMM/attribution with Trade Desk/DV360. Personal care 4.1x TikTok influencers; beverages 2.4x CTV Hulu. North America $249M 2.8x Walmart/Kroger data; EMEA flat €110M 2.3x Snapchat; APAC $85M 2.9x Tmall GlowBeauty; LatAm $18M 2.1x Mercado Libre. AI bidding Criteo +22% CPA cut; GCB Rewards 18M users 3.5x; Amazon clean rooms. Efficiency clawed 150 bps over 3 years to performance, 15% green media. Q4 13.5-14.5%, ROMI 2.5-2.7x for 50 bps share.  

After me, Mike Patel will discuss our supply chain initiatives.  

Mike Patel:  
Thank you, Lisa. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. We are implementing advanced analytics to improve forecasting and inventory management.  

Specifically, on supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings, we generated $285 million run-rate savings in Q3, up 15% from Q2's $248 million, adding 220 bps to 42.8% adjusted gross margin amid 20-30% YoY commodity rises per NielsenIQ. Procurement/sourcing 45% or $128M via Supplier Collaboration 2.0 on SAP Ariba/Palantir AI, 12% TCO cut top 500 SKUs; cocoa forward contracts 18% below spot blockchain sustainable West Africa; EMEA palm hubs 22% lift. Manufacturing 30% $86M, Smart Factory 75% plants OEE +18% to 88% IoT Siemens, 25% downtime cut AquaVibe lines; SKU prune 1,200 cut changeovers 35%, LatAm 10% capacity for 9% volume. Logistics 25% $71M, NextGen Blue Yonder multimodal 11% cut; 40% NA rail shift PepsiCo-style, 22% last-mile; D2S 65% Walmart/Kroger; APAC 16% DC consolidation for 12% e-comm. $1.2B 3-year roadmap to $1B FY26 run-rate, 15% inventory buffer 8.2x turns; Scope 3 -12% regen ag +3% eco pricing GreenGlow. Q4 $300M+, GenAI Q1 +5-7% accuracy for 150 bps margin.  

Finally, Dr. Vasquez will share insights on our innovation pipeline.  

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the progress we are making on our new product development initiatives. Our pipeline is robust, and we are confident that our innovations will drive future growth. Our recent product, Peak Protein bar, is showing promising early results. It has achieved 15% category velocity in its first full quarter, boosted by high-protein formulations tapping into low-calorie snacking trends, contributing to share gains and positioning us for 20% of sales from recent launches by FY25.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions: press star one to queue a question. Our first question comes from Sharon Lee with Goldman Sachs.  

Sharon Lee:  
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?  

Mike Patel:  
Thanks, Sharon. Packaging waste reduction is integral to our supply chain resiliency and sustainability goals. Through our GreenPack initiative and refill programs, we've cut plastic usage 50% in products like UltraClean Pods and HomeShield cleaners, aligning with EU Green Deal mandates and Nielsen's 78% consumer preference for sustainable options. This generated $25 million in savings this quarter from lighter materials and recycled content, part of our $285 million total productivity. We've rolled out refill stations in 25% of European trials at Tesco and Rewe, boosting velocity 15% while trimming logistics costs 11% via optimized multimodal networks. Forward, our 2030 net-zero Scope 3 targets include upcycled packaging across 40% of beverages, de-risking costs as resin prices fluctuate. These efforts not only save 5-7% on procurement TCO but enhance brand loyalty, with eco-claims driving 40% of recent share gains.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan.  

David Kim:  
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?  

Lisa Chen:  
Great question, David. Data analytics is at the heart of our marketing evolution. Our AI-powered predictive bidding with Criteo dynamically allocates 30% of digital budget across 15,000 SKUs, improving CPA 22% and delivering 2.6x ROMI. Through GCB Rewards app with 18 million users, we send hyper-personalized notifications at 3.5x ROI, while clean rooms with Amazon Ads ingest first-party data for privacy-safe targeting. In North America, Walmart Connect and Kroger Precision use shopper data for shelf coupons, lifting NMV 9% for snacks. APAC Tmall on-Tao for GlowBeauty captured 22% under-25 share. MMM with Trade Desk/DV360 attributes real-time, powering TikTok campaigns at 4.1x ROMI via micro-influencers. This personalization boosted conversions 22% on VitalConnect, with digital now 48% of ad spend, driving household penetration up 1.5 points and velocity like 12% for PowerBars.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Our next question comes from Emily Ross with Morgan Stanley.  

Emily Ross:  
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?  

John Ramirez:  
Emily, commodity inflation like cocoa at $10,000/ton all-time highs and palm oil up 20-30% has been a sector challenge, but we've insulated margins effectively. Q3 gross margin expanded 250-280 bps to 53.2-42.1% through 8.4% price/mix realization averaging 9-12% hikes, $285 million productivity, and 70% hedging. Cocoa pass-through via 12-14% snacking uplifts preserved share; palm offsets in Household with 10-11% lists. SupplyFlow AI and Supplier 2.0 cut TCO 12%, with Q4 deflation expected 5-7%. Risks moderated sequentially 15%, supporting FY24 expansion 250-300 bps. Elasticity -0.35 and premium shifts limit volume hit to 2.1%, positioning for sustained 20%+ operating margins.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Our next question comes from Tom Baker with Barclays.  

Tom Baker:  
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thanks, Tom. The landscape is intense with P&G's club pushes, Unilever regen-ag, and private labels at Aldi/Lidl/Walmart gaining, but our 60 bps aggregate gains—11th quarter running—across 85% portfolio show strength. Trends like Ozempic healthification boost our Peak Protein +210 bps NA snacks, Radiance Renew +250 bps prestige beauty vs Lancôme, probiotics +200 bps Health vs Reckitt. Premiumization, e-comm 22% mix, and ESG like 50% less plastic tie to 78% preference, outflanking peers. APAC explosions +180 bps via localized Tmall matcha; Europe fabric +90 bps refills. Category Playbook AI insights, 1.2 points distribution, dynamic pricing yield 65% innovation-driven gains. Q4 50-70 bps targeted, offsetting cocoa risks with $1.2B A&P +8%.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you next quarter.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Vitality Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
